title: CS/SE 1:1 prep - playbook & escalation blueprint
quick_agenda: 30m total: 10m recap customer threads, 10m playbook review, 10m actions/owners
Prioritize safety/regulatory asks for private deployment customers
Confirm next-step timeline for Model X rollback plan
customer_context: Acct: Meridian Health (mid-market). Using Redwood Dedicated for inference. Hit 95th pct latency spikes after patch v2.1.3; SEs traced to a quantization kernel falling back on older CUDA path under heavy batching. Customer is sensitive to downtime (telemetry ingestion) and cost pressures - they are evaluating a 2x throughput uplift with limited budget. Recent ask: tighter observability + automatic fallback after kernel failures.
metrics_snapshot: Last 7d: avg latency 220ms, p95 640ms (above SLA 500ms). Error rate 0.9% (spike on 2026-03-08). Token cost per 1k up 12% due to reprocessing after fallback. Open support CS ticket #CC-218.
content:
Notes to self and conversation prompts:
- Start with quick wins: confirm if they have preflight canary enabled for platform patches (asks: time window, threshold to abort).
- Ask Samir (SE) to explain the kernel fallback chain in 2 sentences for the customer. Need a single-sentence explanation for AO call.
- Bring up Redwood Optimize suggestion: reduce batch max from 64 -> 32 for peak hours as temporary mitigation (estimate 8-12% cost increase, latency improvement for p95).
- Collect specific traces: promise to share 3 representative traces (p95, p99, and a success). Note: attach trace ids from CC-218.
- Draft language for customer: acknowledge, root-cause hypothesis (kernel fallback), mitigation steps (canary/pin, temp batch change, targeted rollback), timeline. Keep it under 5 bullets.
- Reminder: escalate to infra on-call if we see >1% error rate persist for 3h. Use runbook ID: infra-fallback-03.
- Personal to-do before meeting: 1) pull last 48h kernel logs, 2) verify Dedicated capacity headroom, 3) prepare rollback checklist (how to revert v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2 safely).
- Tone: transparent, ops-focused, ownership. Avoid jargon for customer; provide clear next steps and who owns them.
Unresolved questions (for the 1:1):
- Does product want us to offer an automated fallback policy option (region -> model-variant) as a short-term paid add-on?
- Can infra schedule a quick health window to test pinning model variant without impacting other tenants?
- Is there an approved rollback window this week (need legal/hr for maintenance)?
Slack links to prep: #cs-meridian-thread (pin), #se-oncall (for kernel notes).
Reference docs to paste in follow-up: CONFLUENCE-5421 (kernel fallback explainer), runbook infra-fallback-03.
Tone notes for call opener: "We saw a couple of production traces that showed the worst-case behavior; we have a clear mitigation path and a rollback plan. Our priority is to minimize disruption and give you a predictable timeline."
action_items: Olivia: Pull and attach 3 representative traces to CC-218 by 2026-03-11
Samir (SE): Prepare 2-slide explanation of kernel fallback and 1-line customer-friendly summary by meeting
Ravi (Engineering): Confirm Dedicated node headroom and whether we can pin model variant in prod by 2026-03-13
Olivia: Draft customer-facing mitigation plan (5 bullets) and circulate to CS+SE by EOD meeting day
Escalation (if error >1% persists 3h): page infra on-call and start rollback checklist
next_meeting: 2026-03-12 09:00 PT (prep 15m before). Follow-up with customer on 2026-03-13 after patch verification.
notes_to_self: Keep action items small and timeboxed. Offer a single path to rollback + a lower-friction opt-in (reduce batch size) as two parallel mitigations. After call, convert playbook changes into a tiny RFC and add to backlog for Optimize suggestions.
